name: Achromatic ledger
idea: The chrome holds no colour at all; money and counts are set in ink, the one chart hue marks the screen's main data element, and the only other hue is a small signal where a figure changed.
colourBudget: under 1% coloured pixels; the chrome is ink, the one chart hue goes on the main data element, and the only other hue is a small change signal
signature: No brand colour anywhere in the chrome: the one primary action is near-black (a grey pill, #e5e5e5, is the secondary), the main data element (today's series, the booked bars, the current period) takes the one chart hue, #1d5fbf, and everything else is drawn in ink with the comparison or the part after the cursor in grey, zero balances are set in grey, and the only hue on the screen is a small triangle or a short coloured number where a figure changed.
identity: A ground from the product's world in place of #f8f8f8, one level off white and low in chroma: a stone (#f4f3f1) for a bakery or a shop, a sage (#f2f5f2) for a garden or a greenhouse, a blue-grey (#f2f4f7) for a ledger or a meter. Cards stay white; a warm tint stays under the cream check (saturation under about 15%).

The one chart hue (#1d5fbf, or the brand's own hue at 3:1 or more on white) on the screen's main data element: today's line, the booked bars, the current period's column, the margin that breaks. The chrome stays ink and the hue stays under 1% of the screen.
Every figure in Geist Mono, as the style's decision, so money and counts read as a ledger's columns while the text stays Geist.
avoid: a brand-coloured primary button
tinted cards or tinted KPI tiles
a coloured chart where one series in ink says it
bold on anything but money
a chart with no y-scale (the study's one example of this look hid magnitude behind hover and was flagged)
a grey pill as the only button for the screen's main job: in testing an Approve repeated in grey on every row left the screen without a primary
source: taste-skill (desktop study; read the m3 lines for the phone translation)

m3: primary is ink (near-black): filled buttons and the FAB are ink, never the brand hue
secondaryContainer stays a neutral grey, so the NavigationBar indicator and tonal buttons carry no hue
tertiary (the accent) touches only the main data element: today's series, the current period
cards are surfaceContainerLowest on a tinted surface, 0dp elevation, separation by one tone step or a 1dp outlineVariant
positive/negative appear only as a short coloured figure or a small triangle (ExtendedColors)

name: Framed sheet
idea: The app chrome is one tinted L-shaped frame; the work sits on a white sheet with a hairline edge and soft corners, so depth comes from a single tone step and no shadow.
colourBudget: under 3%; the brand shrinks to the logo and a 2px tab underline, the data carries the chroma
signature: One tinted frame holds the sidebar and the 48px top bar with no rule between them; the page is a white sheet inset 8px from the window's right and bottom edges, with a 1px edge, 16px corners and no shadow. The active tab is a 2px underline in ink or the accent; everything else in the chrome is grey.
identity: The frame tinted from the product's colour in place of #f9fbfc: one low-chroma step of its hue (a green-grey for a climate or farm tool, a blue-grey for an observability tool, a stone for a print shop). The sheet stays white.
The brand's own hue from the brief as --chart-1 in place of the dealt teal, on the main series and the one selected state, at 3:1 or more on white, never violet or indigo.
IBM Plex Mono for IDs, keys and the figures in tables (one job): its figures have their own drawing, and a developer reads them as the product's.
avoid: a border between the sidebar and the top bar
a shadow under the sheet
cards whose border is heavier than the sheet's (#cdcfcf on cards read as heavy in the study)
a fourth nesting level: frame, sheet and card are enough
different gutters for the KPI row and the chart row (20 against 24 was flagged)
source: taste-skill (desktop study; read the m3 lines for the phone translation)

m3: the top app bar and NavigationBar sit on one tinted surfaceContainer frame; content sits on a lighter surface sheet with large top corners
no shadows: depth is one tone step
the accent marks the selected tab (2dp indicator) and the main series; the rest of the chrome is grey
IDs, keys and table figures may use a mono face (one job only)

name: Accent ladder
idea: One brand hue at full strength only on small marks, and its pale tints doing all the area work: the active nav row, a plan card, badges and progress tracks.
colourBudget: 3-10%, nearly all of it as pale tints of the one hue
signature: The full hue goes only on small marks: the one filled-button style, the data series and the active nav icon. Its 50-200 tints carry every area: the active nav row (tint fill with the dark ink of the hue), the plan or trial card, badges and progress tracks. The primary action may instead be near-black, as on the study's newsletter home.
identity: The ladder built from the brand's own hue (its logo, the brief's object) in place of the dealt raspberry: the full hue on small marks, its pale tints on areas, never violet or indigo.
The product's objects in the lead block: the newsletter's latest issue as its cover, the shop's products as 40px thumbnails, the course's lessons with their own art.
A ground one level toward the hue's palest tint (#fbf7f8 for the raspberry) in place of #f9fafb, so the page and the tints read as one family.
avoid: the full hue on large areas
a second accent family (four families on one screen was flagged in the study)
a gradient on the trial chip or upgrade button
a left accent bar on the active nav row on top of the tint (seen once in 23 screens)
violet or indigo
source: taste-skill (desktop study; read the m3 lines for the phone translation)

m3: this is Material's own model played straight: the full hue only on small marks (filled button, active icon, data series)
primaryContainer / secondaryContainer tints do all area work: the nav indicator, the plan card, badges, progress tracks
one hue family only; tertiary is reserved for one rare highlight
never the full hue on a large area or a gradient on an upgrade button

name: Editorial greeting
idea: A personal or team home that opens with a typeset greeting in a centred column; every number below it is set at regular weight on tonal panels.
colourBudget: under 2% for the accent; tonal panels carry the structure
signature: The greeting is the h1, in a centred 1100px column on a real 12-column grid (77px columns, 16px gutters), with spans that change by row but share column lines (3/3/3/3, then 9/3, then 6/6, so every internal edge meets one above it). Every figure below is set at regular weight on tonal panels, one layer each: a panel one step off white holds its title and its content directly; a white inner card is used once, for the main chart.
identity: The greeting names this team or household and today's one fact, set from the data ("Morning, Okoro house. The car is ready by 06:10."), never "Welcome back".
Each person's stable hue as a pale tint on their avatar and their own lane or column (a couple and their joint account as three lanes): identity, not data, so it stays out of the chart legends.
A surface from the product's world in place of #f9f9f9, one level toward its material (a sage for a garden, a stone for a kitchen, a blue-grey for a studio), with the page white kept.
avoid: an emoji in the greeting
a tracked uppercase date above the greeting (put the date after it or in the grey line below)
a 624-864px column on a desktop screen (both were flagged as wasted width)
a tray around every card (a grey panel with a white card 6px inside it, on every block, read as a bento template in testing)
red as the accent: in testing red marked a record week of upgrades and read as an alarm; red is for the failing fact only
source: taste-skill (desktop study; read the m3 lines for the phone translation)

m3: the home opens with a typeset greeting in headlineMedium/Large naming this person or household and today's one fact, never "Welcome back" or an emoji
figures at regular weight on tonal surfaceContainer panels, one layer each; one white inner card at most
pill buttons (full shape) and 22-28dp card corners
people get a stable pale hue on their avatar: identity, not data

name: Pastel consumer
idea: Categories are coded by pale tints whose ink is the dark of the same hue, all under one large radius, and each headline sum sits inside the card that explains it.
colourBudget: 5-8%, as pale tiles and data marks
signature: Pale category tiles with the dark of their own hue as ink (#dcf1ff with #0a3a80), one large radius (20px on cards, stepping down to 10, 8 and 5 inside), and quiet money polarity: income green with a plus sign, spending in ink, no red on ordinary outgoings. Tints go on small tiles, avatars and chips; a panel that holds a list stays white. When the product has people (two partners, a family), each gets one hue, at least 60 degrees from the next.
identity: The tile hues from the account's own colours (the card's colour, each pot's colour in the app) in place of the dealt cobalt, each tile pale with the dark of its own hue as ink.
The money's own objects: the card art at its real ratio, merchant marks at 24px in the rows, the goal's picture on its pot.
Manrope's figures carry the balance: 30-36px at 600 with tabular figures and the pence in a smaller grey, so the number itself is the face.
avoid: a gradient balance card
two data palettes on one page (flagged in the study)
red on every outgoing amount
a 624px phone-width column on a desktop screen (flagged as a stretched phone screen)
a KPI strip on top: the sums belong in their cards
whole panels tinted per person or category beside white cards (two surface languages on one screen)
source: taste-skill (desktop study; read the m3 lines for the phone translation)

m3: category tiles are pale containers with the dark of their own hue as ink (primary/secondary/tertiaryContainer + on*Container, plus ExtendedColors for more categories)
one large radius family: 20dp cards stepping down to 12/8dp inside
quiet money polarity: income in success with a plus sign, spending in onSurface, no red on ordinary outgoings
balances in a figure face with tabular figures; the minor unit smaller and grey

name: True-black flat
idea: Night mode on true black: sidebar, top bar and page share one ground, elevation is a lightness step alone, and colour is confined to data marks.
colourBudget: at or under 3%; the accent never touches buttons, tabs or nav
signature: Elevation by lightness alone (#000 ground, #111 card, #2a2a2a nested panel) with no borders or shadows on cards; the active nav item is marked only by its label going from #bbb to #fff; the primary control is made primary by inversion, a white 36px pill with black text.
identity: The one data hue from the product's world in place of the dealt lime: a solar amber (#f2b33d) for an energy home, a sky blue (#4cb3f0) for water or weather, a lime only for sport. It is still the only hue on data and never touches buttons, tabs or nav. A green or yellow-green hue is also --positive; an amber that sits beside --warning leaves the warning to its pill pair.

A ground with the product's temperature: the studied #000 for media and events, a warm near-black (#0e0d0c) for a home, a cool one (#0c0d0f) for a monitor, with cards one lightness step above it (#181716, #15171a). Never navy or slate.

A signature element from the product's world as the lead: the energy home's power flow (sun, house, battery and grid with their live kW), an event's doors against capacity, an artist's release with its cover.
avoid: a navy or slate dark theme
glow, neon borders or shadows
a hue per chart (five hues across four charts was flagged)
the accent on buttons, tabs or nav
a 64px top bar left empty across most of its width (flagged twice)
source: taste-skill (desktop study; read the m3 lines for the phone translation)

m3: dark scheme on true black (#000 background/surface), elevation by lightness steps of surfaceContainer only, no borders, no shadows
primary is inverted ink: a white pill with black text
the accent hue lives only on data marks (tertiary), never on buttons, tabs or the nav indicator
NavigationBar indicator is a neutral surfaceContainerHighest; the active label goes from onSurfaceVariant to onSurface
still ship a light scheme: the user chooses, not the style

name: Data terminal
idea: A research or monitoring screen read in long sessions: cards darker than the ground, tabular digits that stack, signs instead of colour, and every selection marked by the same 1px accent line.
colourBudget: under 3%; the accent is never more than a 1px line
signature: Every selection (tab, toggle, range, nav item) is a 1px accent line exactly as wide as its label, placed on the nearest existing edge; numbers stay white or grey and carry their sign in the text ('+$24,000,000').
identity: Every figure in a monospace as the style's decision (IBM Plex Mono or JetBrains Mono for each price, count and time, digits that stack), with the text in Public Sans.
The one accent line from the product's world in place of the dealt blue (the exchange's or the team's hue): still the only selection mark, never violet or indigo.
A signature of the market or the system as the lead: an order book's depth as two mirrored bar lists, an incident as a minute-by-minute strip, a region map with the list beside it.
avoid: filled pill tabs or a coloured segmented control
a chart with no scale and no dates (the studied screen had none and was flagged)
tertiary text under 4.5:1 (#4c4c4f read at about 2:1 in the study)
lighter cards with borders and a glow
green and red on every number; the one column whose job is "what moved today" and a negative headline figure may carry the polarity colours
source: taste-skill (desktop study; read the m3 lines for the phone translation)

m3: for screens read in long sessions: figures in a mono face with tabular digits, signs in the text (+24,000) not only colour
selection is one accent line (2dp indicator) under tabs and segmented choices; no filled pills in content
cards may sit darker than the background (surfaceContainerLowest)
secondary text keeps 4.5:1: onSurfaceVariant, never a dimmer custom grey

name: Tonal Material, decided
idea: Material You played with conviction instead of by default: one brand hue drives every tonal container, surfaces step by tone not shadow, and one signature shape or motion belongs to this product alone.
colourBudget: 5-12%, nearly all of it as tonal containers; the full hue only on the one primary action and active states
signature: The brand hue shows up as primaryContainer surfaces (the hero status card, the nav indicator, selected chips), never as a large saturated area; the hero of the main screen is a single tonal card that answers the screen's question in one figure or sentence; one expressive shape (a cut corner, a blob, a squircle) appears exactly once per screen as the product's mark.
identity: The hue from the product's own world (a scanner's laser red, a water app's river teal), checked at 3:1 on surface, never the baseline purple #6750A4.
One signature element only this product has (a cleaner's freed-space figure, a step counter's route sketch) as the hero.
A brand face on display and headline roles only; body stays on the text face.
avoid: the baseline M3 purple scheme
dynamic color as the only identity (ship a branded static scheme; dynamic is an opt-in)
every screen a column of identical Cards
elevation shadows on cards

m3: default M3 roles: primary for the one action, primaryContainer for the hero card and selected states, secondaryContainer for the nav indicator and chips, tertiary for one rare highlight
surfaces: surface for the screen, surfaceContainerLow for grouped content, no shadows
dynamic color offered as a setting with the branded scheme as default

name: Media canvas
idea: The user's content is the interface: photos, video and art run edge to edge, and the chrome recedes to neutral dark surfaces and scrims that appear only when needed.
colourBudget: under 2% in the chrome; the content supplies all the colour
signature: Content full-bleed under transparent system bars; controls sit on a gradient-free scrim (surface at 60-80% alpha) or a floating toolbar; the accent marks only the active tool and the export/save action; the content grid has no gutters wider than 2dp.
identity: An accent from the product's craft (a film-stock amber, a darkroom red, a neon for a wallpaper app), only on the active tool and the primary action.
The user's own latest work as the hero of the home screen, never a stock sample.
Tool icons drawn as one family (Material Symbols Rounded or Sharp, one weight), labelled under the icon in labelSmall.
avoid: colourful chrome competing with the content
cards with borders around thumbnails
controls permanently over the content with no way to hide them
a light theme forced on an editor (offer it, default dark)

m3: edge-to-edge with transparent system bars over content; insets applied to controls, not to the content
bottom tool row (horizontally scrolling) + ModalBottomSheet for a tool's parameters
NavigationBar only on browse screens; hidden in editor/viewer
secondaryContainer neutral; primary = accent for the one primary action (Save/Export)

name: Playful rounded
idea: Saturated pastel fields, big radii and springy motion for apps whose job is encouragement: progress feels like a reward, never a dashboard.
colourBudget: 15-30% as pale fields; saturated hue only on progress and the one action
signature: Three hue families as pale containers (primary/secondary/tertiaryContainer) coding sections or subjects; one bold progress element tied to the real goal; buttons as full pills with a 2dp darker bottom edge; spring motion with a gentle overshoot on success only.
identity: A mascot or drawn character only if the product has one; never a generic emoji.
Subject colours from the content itself (math = one hue, reading = another), consistent everywhere.
A rounded display face; body text stays a highly legible sans at bodyLarge.
avoid: confetti on every action
progress rings standing in for real content
more than three hue families
text on saturated fields under 4.5:1

m3: full-pill buttons and 28-36dp card corners (Shapes.extraLarge)
MotionScheme.expressive() where available (material3 1.4+), else springs with dampingRatio 0.6-0.7 on success moments only
NavigationBar with labels always visible; icons filled when selected
